reasons.R7: The workflow design is secure and sensible, but MAX_VERDICTS is 100 while the description promises 300 and the validation script has no tests, so it needs changes.

A well-scoped, opt-in flag with a spoof-resistant sentinel and thorough parametrized tests; only minor nits remain (drive-by reformatting in the test files, unparenthesized and/or precedence, a TypeAdapter validation on every failure).

A test-only pin of existing behaviour that adds unit tests and a negative corpus case, with the doc counts and baseline regenerated the way the repo's conventions require, so it is safe to merge as-is.
A focused fix that stops discovered rules from being passed back to the SDK, with updated snapshots and a new regression assertion on instructionDirectories.
It is a focused, well-reasoned fix for both stale-search bugs using a standard onChange-ref pattern, held back only by the lack of automated tests.
A clean refactor that changes no behavior: it puts SOURCE_MODES in one place, mirrors the change into every synced copy and adds changelog and README entries, so it can merge as-is.
The nil guard is correct, but the diff also adds a stale-connection early return in OpcodeDispatch that the description never mentions and that changes listener behavior, and there are no tests.

Sound behavior-preserving extraction of duplicated guard and lookup code backed by existing suites, with minor nits (double kody_id normalization in app-fetch, an odd inline rewrite of the subscription superRefine) that don't block merge.

The changeset grouping works and is tested, but GET requests are not rejected inside changesets, the whole mixed batch is parsed with transaction semantics, and the PR bundles an unrelated CI runner pin and README edit, so it needs changes.

Coherent mock-compliance changes with a safe owner-name fallback and backend test coverage, but a stacked PR mixing backend schema and several UI tweaks with only backend assertions merits a careful review before merging.

Scoping the umask in a subshell plus an explicit Squid umask fixes the unreadable-log issue with meaningful regression tests, though the shell-extraction tests are somewhat brittle and partly simulate the umask they verify.

A well-scoped transport retry that only retries idempotent GETs and connect errors and skips timeouts, with URL-free error messages and a regression test that reproduces the dropped connection; mergeable with at most minor nits.

The rename and reference updates are consistent, but running `node check-employee-service.ts` relies on Node type stripping, which is not available on every Node version, and the focused tests were never actually run, so it needs verification before merge.
A small, well-explained NumPy pin that fixes the CI import failure; the new test only checks the exact install call sequence and stubs the git module globally, but it is acceptable.
A focused, low-risk change that surfaces error causes without changing retry behaviour, though it adds no tests for the new error messages.
A small, targeted build plugin that fixes the codepage issue at the right stage; it has no automated test and was not checked in Premiere on a non-UTF-8 locale.

The sweep now runs in bounded, SKIP LOCKED, MATERIALIZED-CTE batches with continuations deleted first, the sqlc code is regenerated to match, and a DB-backed test covers the multi-batch and locked-row cases, so it is ready to merge.
A minimal, correct fix to the duplicated description in both the command and the docs, with a focused test that would fail without it.

The declarative fix is sound and well tested, but the deeply nested Jinja predicate is repeated in two places, and the IGNORE response filter only checks data[0], so a reviewer would likely ask for a simplification first.

A focused, well-documented security dependency bump that follows the existing uv cooldown/pin pattern and makes the one test adjustment the OTel type change requires; the main residual risk is the OTel minor-version jump, which only existing suites cover.

The refactor into decideAction is clean, but the PR depends on an SDK bump that hasn't been published, so the server typecheck fails; it also never checks approval.actionId against the action, and the new verified-approval hook path has no tests.

A focused, well-tested escape for saves that won't start, with a sensible guest-time wake budget; the only extras are the plans/README note and the regenerated service-worker hashes, so it is close to mergeable as-is.
Minimal, well-explained test isolation fix that copies tree-project into tmp_path, removing the xdist race with a clear comment.

Fixes the root cause by remapping preview fileIds to paths in the docs config and translations, with focused unit tests and a changelog; the only small risk is that any bare string that happens to equal a fileId also gets rewritten.
A focused, hash-verified, add-only trust-store fix that I'd merge, though there's no automated check and the build now fetches from the network.
Small, opt-in change that follows the existing _apply_* pattern and has focused tests; the only gap is that dedupe misses specs like 'path:path' without rwm, which is minor.

It solves the billing problem and has thorough tests, but it enables a behavior-changing preflight by default, reorders cleanup and drops a progress event, and uses dense code that drifts from the repo's style, so it needs another review pass.
A clean dead-code removal that deletes the two unused helpers and only their own tests, with a repo-wide grep showing nothing else calls them, so it can merge as-is.
Clean, self-contained docs component wired in through an optional slot, with accessible mobile handling. There are no automated tests, which is acceptable for a docs homepage tweak.
Well-scoped, backward-compatible lookback_window option with good unit tests, docs, and a version bump; mergeable after a live prerelease check of the non-DAY custom report granularities.
Reasonable, well-verified layout fix reusing existing Opal primitives, but there are no automated tests and it relies on a long arbitrary Tailwind class plus a verbose comment.
Small, focused change that routes the setting-query HTTP responses through the existing handler with a parser test, though the loadConfigValues wiring itself is untested.

A well-reasoned fix that passes real Split.Column/Split.Inspector elements to the host, with targeted tests and a changeset; it was not verified on a device with v5, and it accepts the documented SafeAreaProvider tradeoff.

Solid approach with good tests, but it reaches into private retriever internals, changes shared requester state while the check runs, makes every transient error propagate during check, and its internal message wrongly says exit_on_rate_limit; it needs another round.

A well-scoped fix with focused tests that moves disk resizing to upgrade-instance and fails fast on the misleading flag; the only nits are the regex trick that capitalizes the prompt and the loosely typed risk-registry string.

A clean, focused removal of an unused NAPI class. Both binding copies were updated consistently, but they were edited by hand and the change has not been verified on the native build or CI, so it needs a quick CI confirmation before merging.
A clean, focused move of Delete into the header that keeps the same permission, paused and tooltip logic, with the e2e page object updated; the added 30s timeout is a minor oddity.
It reuses the existing UID/GID-aware helper, has good tests and updated docs, but the accessSync gate on .copilot needs a check that it matches the absent-directory case.
A focused, well-tested validation that fails before the indexer is queried; it is mergeable, with only a small cost from always fetching server info up front.
Minimal mechanical lint and deprecation fixes that behave the same as before and unblock CI, so I would merge as-is.
The preflight short-circuit sits correctly after all validation and before any recording or execution, and it is well tested, but merging depends on the upstream sms-kit change being deployed first.
A well-sourced adjudication doc with a changelog entry and a pinning test that matches the repo's conventions; the test only guards existing behavior and the prose is dense.

Clean fallback to the workflow environment with tests and refreshed locks, but making activation inherit the environment's protection rules could add a second approval gate, and that should be confirmed before merging.
Focused, correct path confinement (realpath plus separator-terminated prefix check) with load-bearing tests for traversal, symlink, prefix-sibling and root cases.
A focused, well-explained fix for a flaky test that reuses an existing fake-timer pattern and restores real timers afterward; it is fine to merge, give or take a small cleanup.

It is a small, correct check that runs before a packet ID is allocated and has a regression test that would fail without it; the only nits are the repeated magic number and a heavy 70k-iteration loop.
A small, focused refactor that swaps the dead_code allows for cfg(test) gating and removes unused helpers without changing production behavior; I'd merge it as-is.
Unwrapping parens before comparison cleanly fixes the asymmetric case with good test coverage, though the extra-parenthesized golden autofix output is a bit odd.

A well-tested native Reco guardrail that follows the existing GenericGuardrailAPI and registry pattern with safe fail-closed defaults, needing only minor style polish (heavy Final and pyright annotations).
A clean dead-code removal that moves the test-only frontier into a cfg(test) impl so the parity tests keep their coverage, though it could not be built or tested locally and depends on macOS CI.
A clean provider hook with an unchanged default, all six call sites updated consistently, and focused unit and handler tests that would fail without the change, so it is ready to merge.
A clean consolidation of two duplicated safe loaders into one shared helper that keeps the same behavior, with a test that confirms python tags are rejected.

This is a well-structured end-to-end change (Rust chat.update endpoint, regenerated client, desktop ref storage with bounded eviction and safe no-duplicate failure) with good engine tests, held back only by missing Rust/delivery-client tests and the extra settings reads in the rerun checks.

The marker addition and the dedup logic in the enhancer are reasonable and tested. But the PR also bundles unrelated changes: it loosens a performance test (retained 300->100, depth 8) and refactors slice building in Go, both of which should be split out or justified.

The memoization is well designed and tested, but sharing mutable root-frame maps across runs depends on ownShape guarding every write path, which this diff doesn't fully show (for example, writes to unvalued when a value is assigned), so it needs a careful review before merging.

A narrowly scoped CI fix that pins the version and checksum in source, regenerates the lock file consistently, and extends the existing pin contract test to cover the reporter workflow, matching the established pattern.
Moving the vision filter so it runs for every routing strategy is sound and well tested, but the bundled maybe_get_model_id metadata change widens scope and reads caller-supplied metadata.
A small, idiomatic fix: defaulting showClearButton to undefined stops Vue from casting the missing Boolean prop to false, and the regression tests cover both the default and the explicit opt-out.

A small, correct change that puts source first in the server-side sort and adds per-section dividers, with a cross-page backend test and doc updates; only the frontend dividers (including the federated one) lack automated coverage.

A well-structured, spec-driven feature with good unit tests and a changelog entry; the only minor issues are the duplicated email-check code and that the interactive prompt path in binding.rs isn't tested end to end.

Correct same-engine-only target inheritance with deep-copied maps plus needs-dependency scanning and focused table tests; the target-walking logic is a bit duplicated and verbose but it's mergeable with only minor polish.
A small, well-targeted limit increase that keeps the other hardening settings and adds regression tests for both network modes; mergeable as-is.
